AnimationKeyframeEditor.Buttons.Rotate.T: Rotate the selected bones with the gizmo
AnimationKeyframeEditor.Buttons.ResetPos: Put the current frame back the way it was when the animation was loaded. Not possible on an added frame
AnimationKeyframeEditor.PasteOptions.Tit: Which parts of each bone the pastes and the interpolation change

AnimationKeyframeEditor.Buttons.PasteGlo: Paste the clipboard's frames from the current frame on
AnimationKeyframeEditor.Buttons.PasteSel: Paste the clipboard's frames from the current frame on, into the selected bones only
AnimationKeyframeEditor.Interpolation.In: Set frames A and B, go to a frame between them, then drag the slider: that frame's pose blends from A's (left) to B's (right)

AnimationKeyframeEditor.Interpolation.Ap: Set the current frame to the slider's blend of frames A and B

MountAnimationCreator.Title: Rider Animation Editor
MountAnimationCreator.Intro: Makes mounted rider animation sets. Load the rider and the mount in the Rider and Mount panels above, and pick their animation sets and slots there. Picking a mount slot also picks the rider slot of the same name (RIDER_ and the mount slot).
MountAnimationCreator.Kinds.Synchronized: the rider's animroot moves with the mount's and the rider sits at saddle height, like the Empire horse riders.
MountAnimationCreator.Kinds.Attached.Inf: war beast riders. The rider's animroot stays at the origin, and the game glues it to an attach bone (ap_) of the mount's tech skeleton, like the Kislev horse riders. The tech skeleton is an .anim in a tech folder next to the mount's meshes.
MountAnimationCreator.Tabs.MountChange.T: Refit a synchronized rider set made for one mount onto another, still synchronized: a horse rider's set onto a cold one, say
MountAnimationCreator.Tabs.AttachedMount: Move an attached (war beast) rider set made for one mount onto another, still attached
MountAnimationCreator.Tabs.AttachConvers: Convert rider animations between synchronized and attached, on the same mount
MountAnimationCreator.MountChange.Intro: Refits a synchronized rider set to a different mount. In the Rider panel, pick the rider set made for the old mount; in the Mount panel, load the new mount and pick its set. The rider bone below is glued to a point on the new mount, on every frame of the new mount's animation for the same slot.
MountAnimationCreator.RiderAttachment.Ri: The rider bone glued to the mount. Usually root, the pelvis
MountAnimationCreator.RiderAttachment.Mo: The point of the new mount the rider bone is glued to
MountAnimationCreator.RiderAttachment.No: Select a vertex of the mount first: click the mount in the viewport, press F3 for vertex selection and click a vertex.
MountAnimationCreator.RiderAttachment.Ve: To pick the vertex: click the mount in the viewport, press F3 for vertex selection, click a vertex on the saddle, then Set. F1 goes back to object selection.
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.Set.ToolTi: Use the vertex selected in the viewport
MountAnimationCreator.Settings.FitAnimat: Stretch to the mount animation's length
Resample the rider animation to the mount animation's frame count and duration. Off: frames are matched one to one
MountAnimationCreator.Settings.LoopCount: How many times the rider animation plays back to back before it's fitted to the mount. 1 plays it once
MountAnimationCreator.Settings.TransOffs: Moves the rider bone away from the vertex, in metres (X, Y, Z)
MountAnimationCreator.Settings.RotOffset: Turns the rider bone, in degrees (yaw, pitch, roll)
MountAnimationCreator.Settings.Scale.Too: Scales the mount, and with it where the vertex is
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.UpdatePrev: Refit the picked slot's rider animation again. It also updates by itself whenever a slot, the vertex or a setting changes
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.SaveCurren: Save the picked slot's refitted animation next to the rider animation, named with the output prefix
MountAnimationCreator.MountChange.WholeS: Refits every RIDER_ animation of the rider set whose slot the new mount's set has, against that slot's mount animation, and saves a new rider set for the new mount. Slots that play the same on any mount, and slots the new mount doesn't have, are kept.
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedMountChang: Moves an attached rider set to a different mount. In the Rider panel, pick the attached rider set made for the old mount; in the Mount panel, load the new mount and pick its set. The game puts attached riders on the new mount's attach bone, so the animations carry over as they are, unless they're stretched to the new mount's animations or offset below. The set's synchronized slots (deaths and RIDER_COMBAT_ kills) are copied unchanged; refit any that look wrong one at a time in the Synchronized Mount Change tab.
Pick the new mount's tech skeleton to see the rider on its attach bone. It's only used for the preview.
Moves the rider away from the attach bone, in metres (X, Y, Z)
Turns the rider around the attach bone, in degrees (yaw, pitch, roll)

Makes a new rider set for the new mount. Every attached RIDER_ animation whose slot the new mount's set has is stretched and offset with these settings, or kept when that changes nothing. Synchronized slots, and slots the new mount doesn't have, are kept.
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.RefitSet: Refit the whole rider set to this mount
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.RefitSet.T: Make a new rider set for the mount in the Mount panel, with these settings. Saved with the refitted animations, as a new animpack in animations\database\battle\bin
MountAnimationCreator.Batch.NameTitle: Name of the new animation set
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.Hel: Converts a rider set, or the picked slot, between synchronized and attached, on the same mount. The preview shows the converted animation where the game would.
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.Tec: The mount skeleton with the attach bones added
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.Bro: Pick the mount's tech skeleton. Only tech folders are listed, for example variantmeshes\wh_variantmodels\hr1\emp\emp_warbeast_horse\tech
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.Att: The bone the rider's animroot is glued to, usually ap_riderposition_0
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.NoA: {0} has no ap_ bones. The attach bone is in the mount's tech skeleton, in a tech folder next to its meshes.
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.Wro: The tech skeleton doesn't fit the mount
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.ToAttached: Convert the picked rider slot's animation to attached, against the mount slot's animation. Slots picked after this are converted too
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.ToSynchron: Convert the picked rider slot's animation to synchronized, against the mount slot's animation. Slots picked after this are converted too
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.SaveConver: Save the converted animation next to the rider animation, named with the output prefix
MountAnimationCreator.AttachedRiders.Who: Converts every RIDER_ animation of the rider set whose slot the mount set has, against that slot's mount animation, and saves a new animation set with them. Animations already in that mode are kept, and so are deaths and the RIDER_COMBAT_ kills, which vanilla attached sets keep synchronized.
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.SetToAttac: Make an attached copy of the rider set. Saved with the new animations, as a new animpack in animations\database\battle\bin
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.SetToSynch: Make a synchronized copy of the rider set. Saved with the new animations, as a new animpack in animations\database\battle\bin
Saved animations go next to the animation they were made from, with this in front of the name. New sets start with it too
MountAnimationCreator.Labels.AnimVersion: The .anim version to save. Warhammer III uses 7
MountAnimationCreator.Labels.EnsureUniqu: Never overwrite: number the name if it's taken
Add a number to the name when a file of that name exists. Off: overwrite it
MountAnimationCreator.Visualisation.Disp: The preview is the red rider: the animation being made or converted
Show the red preview rider's skeleton
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.CopyRiderA: Copy the preview for the Keyframe Editor
Copy every frame of the preview to the clipboard. In the Keyframe Editor, Paste under Copy between Keyframe Editors puts them into the animation open there, to touch them up before saving
MountAnimationCreator.CopyForKeyframeEdi: There's no preview to copy yet.
MountAnimationCreator.Buttons.Reset.Tool: Close this tool and open an empty one in its place: no models, animations or settings
MountAnimationCreator.Reset.Confirm: Start over with an empty Rider Animation Editor? Anything not saved is lost.

SuperView.Edit3D.RedoTooltip: Redo the last move or turn undone in this tab's file

SuperView.Problems.NonFiniteTime: Its start or end time is not a number

SuperView.Problems.MissingPropAnimation: Animation not in the loaded packs, drawn without it: {0}
SuperView.Problems.MissingPropSkeleton: No skeleton {0} for the prop's animation, drawn without it
SuperView.Problems.MissingAnimation: Animation not in the loaded packs: {0}

SuperView.Problems.NoAnimationBin: Pick an animation bin to preview the docking
SuperView.Problems.MissingDockSlot: The animation bin has no {0} animation to dock with
SuperView.Problems.MissingDockBone: The skeleton has none of the bones {0}
SuperView.MissingMeta.NotInPacks: The animation bin names this META file, but it is not in any loaded pack:
SuperView.MissingMeta.CreateTooltip: Writes an empty META file at this path in the editable pack, so tags can be added to it
SuperView.MissingMeta.NotNamedAnimation: No META file is named for this animation, so it has no tags to show.
SuperView.MissingMeta.NotNamedPersistent: The animation bin names no persistent META file.
SuperView.EffectPreview.Tooltip: What the game supplies while the unit plays. Used only for this preview, never written into the META
SuperView.EffectPreview.DistanceCulledTo: Hides EFFECT tags marked Distance Culled, as the game does for a unit far from the camera
SuperView.EffectPreview.AuraTooltip: The wind-up vfx on the caster's body while casting a spell. Cast animations carry EFFECT tags of type ability_aura (1) as placeholders, and the game plays the spell's wind_up_aura_vfx (special_ability_displays) there instead. Empty, they play the vfx they name
SuperView.EffectPreview.WeaponTooltip: The wind-up vfx in the caster's hand or staff while casting a spell. Cast animations carry EFFECT tags of type ability_weapon (2) as placeholders, and the game plays the spell's wind_up_weapon_vfx (special_ability_displays) there instead. Not the unit's weapon effects. Empty, they play the vfx they name

ImportWindow.Title: ImportWindow
RmvToGltfImporter.ConvertMaterialMap: Convert Material Map From Blender To TW format
RmvToGltfImporter.ConvertNormalMap: Convert Normal Map From Blue To Orange Type
RmvToGltfImporter.KeySamplesPerSecond: Number of Key Samples Per Second
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.ImportMeshes: Convert every mesh and primitive in the glTF scene into an RMV2 mesh.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.ImportMateria: Convert the textures the glTF materials use into game DDS files.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.NewSkeletonNa: Name of the new skeleton made for files without a //skeleton// marker. Defaults to the skin, armature or file name. No paths or characters that aren't valid in file names.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.SourceForward: The axis the source asset faces. Standard glTF faces +Z; Unreal/PSK assets face +X. The importer doesn't guess from names or shapes.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.AutoScaleHuma: For skeletons made from the file's own skin: measure head and feet in the bind pose and scale the model, skeleton and animation translations to the game's humanoid01 size. Off keeps the glTF size.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.ConvertMateri: Rearrange the channels of a Blender metallic/roughness texture into the game's material map layout.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.ConvertNormal: Convert a blue normal map (Blender, Substance Painter) into the orange two-channel type Total War uses.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.ImportAnimati: Import every animation in the glTF; each one becomes its own .anim file.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.AutoDetectAni: Use the frame rate of the glTF's evenly spaced keys, so animations Blender baked at the scene rate aren't resampled again. Falls back to the value below when it can't be detected.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.KeySamplesPer: Key frames sampled per second of animation. Must be greater than 0.
RmvToGltfImporter.Tooltips.OverwriteExis: Replace files the import writes that already exist in the pack. When off, the import stops and writes nothing if any of them exist.

RmvToGltfExporter.Tooltips.ConvertMateri: Convert the Material texture into the version Blender prefers
RmvToGltfExporter.Tooltips.ConvertNormal: Convert the normal map texture into blue version - used by a lot of software, including blender
AudioProjectConverter.Title: Audio Project Converter
AudioProjectConverter.Description: The Audio Project Converter is a tool for creating an Audio Project out of Dialogue Events in the provided .bnk files. It takes the VO Actor substring(s) and searches the Dialogue Events in the supplied .bnk files for their usage and converts that to the Audio Project format. Read the tooltips for more information.
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.AudioProj: The name of your converted Audio Project.
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.OutputDir: The pack directory where the converted Audio Project is output to. There needs to be a file in the directory for it to show.
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.VoActorSu: A substring common to all the VO Actor keys whose usage you want converted to the Audio Project format. You can include multiple substrings using a comma to separate them e.g. "ovn_vo_actor_Araby, ovn_vo_actor_Albion".
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.WemsDirec: A directory on your computer containing all the .wem files used in the soundbank (just use all wem files if you don't know which are used).
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.BnksDirec: A directory on your computer containing all the .bnk files to be searched.
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.Convertin: Tick this box if you need to get the States used in the soundbank from the Wwise project. There's no need to tick if you're converting a vanilla .bnk or the pack has a states_data.dat in the pack for the .bnk you're converting as that contains the States data for a or .bnk made by the Audio Editor.
AudioProjectConverter.Tooltips.Soundbank: The path to the SoundbanksInfo.xml should be "your_wwise_project_folder\GeneratedSoundBanks\Windows\SoundbanksInfo.xml". This contains the States data for the Wwise project.
AudioProjectMerger.Title: Audio Project Merger
AudioProjectMerger.Description: The Audio Project Merger is a tool for merging two Audio Projects.
AudioProjectMerger.Tooltips.MergedAudioP: The name of your merged Audio Project.
AudioProjectMerger.Tooltips.OutputDirect: The pack directory where the merged Audio Project is output to. There needs to be a file in the directory for it to show.
AudioProjectMerger.Tooltips.BaseAudioPro: The path to the Audio Project that you want to merge the Merging Audio Project into.
AudioProjectMerger.Tooltips.MergingAudio: The path to the Audio Project that you want to merge into the base Audio Project.
DialogueEventMerger.Title: Dialogue Event Merger
DialogueEventMerger.Description: The Dialogue Event Merger is a tool for merging Dialogue Events from modded SoundBanks with Dialogue Events from vanilla into a single SoundBank. Read the tooltips for more information.
DialogueEventMerger.Tooltips.SoundBankSu: The suffix of your merged SoundBanks.
DialogueEventMerger.Tooltips.ModdedSound: Select one or more modded SoundBanks from which their Dialogue Events will be merged with vanilla.
NewAudioProject.Title: New Audio Project
NewAudioProject.Name: Name
NewAudioProject.Tooltips.Name: The name of the Audio Project.
NewAudioProject.Tooltips.Location: The folder location in the Pack the Audio Project should go.
NewAudioProject.Tooltips.Language: The game language of your Audio Project.

AnimationReTarget.Batch.Error.SkeletonsR: Select a source and a target skeleton first.
AnimationReTarget.Batch.Error.InvalidSpe: The animation speed multiplier must be greater than 0.
AnimationReTarget.Batch.Error.MappingReq: No bones are mapped. Set up the bone mapping first.
AnimationReTarget.Batch.Error.NoCandidat: No animations were found for the source skeleton.
AnimationReTarget.Batch.Error.SourceFold: The animation is not in a folder: {0}

KitbashTool.SaveDialog.Tooltips.Regenera: Writes every material from Asset Editor's template for this save, also the ones it would otherwise keep as they were loaded. A material file at the name Asset Editor gives it is overwritten when only this model uses it.

AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.ContainerT: The Container Type determines the order in which objects are played.
Sequence - Plays objects in the sequence in which they were added.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.RandomType: The Container Type determines the order in which objects are played.
Shuffle - Plays objects at random without repeating an object until the entire pool of objects has been played.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.Repetition: Repitition Interval determines how many other objects must be played before an object can be repeated.
If Random Type is Standard, the object played is selected completely randomly, but the last n objects played are excluded from the list.
If Random Type is Shuffle, when the container is looped, the last n objects played will be excluded from the list.
If Random Type is Shuffle, non-looping and Play Mode continuous, the Repetition Interval has no effect on the playback of the container.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.PlaylistEn: Playlist End Behaviour determines how the container behaves after it has played the last object in the playlist.
Restart - Plays the playlist in the same order.
Play In Reverse Order - Plays the playlist in reverse order.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.PlayModeLi: The Play Mode determines whether a single object or the full playlist is played when triggered.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.PlayModeSt: Step - Plays one object in the playlist when triggered.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.PlayModeCo: Continuous - Plays the complete playlist when triggered.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.AlwaysRese: Always Reset Container determines whether playback continues or returns to the start of the playlist when a container is replayed after being stopped during playback.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.LoopingTyp: The Looping Type handles how many times a container is played.
Disabled - The container does not loop playback.
Finite Looping - The container playback loops according to the Number of Loops.
Infinite Looping - The container playback loops infinitely.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.NumberOfLo: The Number of Loops determines how many times a container is played if Looping Type is set to Finite Looping.
AudioEditor.Settings.Tooltips.Transition: The Transition Type handles the transition between objects in the container.
Xfade (amp) - Adds a crossfade between two objects using constant amplitude.
Xfade (power) - Adds a crossfade between two objects using constant power.
Delay - Adds a silence between two objects.
Sample accurate - Creates seamless transitions with no latency between objects.
Trigger rate - Determines the rate at which new objects within the container will be played. This option is useful for simulating rapid gun fire.

Transition Duration is the length of the crossfades or delay between clips. If Trigger rate is selected as the transition type, the duration defines the amount of time that will pass before the next sound is triggered.
The Duration slider is unavailable when the Sample Accurate option is selected.

The range is between 0 and 3600 seconds. The maximum duration of a crossfade is equal to half the duration of the sound. In cases where the crossfade time is longer than half the duration of the sound, the crossfade duration is automatically adjusted to the maximum allowed. This automatic adjustment is performed by the sound engine at run time. Wwise does not limit or indicate that the crossfade time is too long for some of the sounds in the container.

CampaignAnimationSetEditor.AddStatus.Pic: Pick a known vanilla status, or type a custom/modded name.
CampaignAnimationSetEditor.BattleFragmen: If this set has flying animations (FLY_STAND etc.), they're used by default. Check this to always use the ground moveset instead - e.g. if you want a flying unit to walk around the campaign map rather than fly. Has no effect on a unit with no flying animations to begin with.
Freeze root bone for rider animations

Only applies if the selected set is detected as a rider (mounted) skeleton. Some older-style mount rigs bake the mount's movement into every animation - not just locomotion - and need the root bone zeroed across the board to sit still on the campaign map. Most Warhammer 3 rider rigs are already authored in place and don't need this, so it defaults to off.

CampaignAnimationSetEditor.TypeColumnToo: Which status this animation was originally authored for. Rows often show a different value than the status they live under - a row inside status_battle commonly shows Type=status_normal, meaning it reuses status_normal's authored animation. Vanilla files only ever use "global" or "status_normal" here.
